# Hierarchical-Complexity @ Stage 6 — Nominal & Rule

> developed 2026-07-26. Deepened from 74 to 140+ lines.

## Expression on this line

Hierarchical-complexity at Order 4 is **rule-governed hierarchy**: the first moment
where the agent follows structural rules not because监督 is present but because the
rules have been internalized as "the way we organize things." The child builds towers
according to the rules because "that's how you build properly," not because a teacher
is watching. The artisan follows the master's structural technique because it is the
technique, not because the master is watching.

The key advance from Stage 5 is **norm internalization**. The structural rule is no
longer external — it is part of the agent's identity. Breaking the rule produces guilt,
not just fear of punishment. This is the birth of structural morality: the sense that
some ways of organizing are right and others are wrong.

Structural rules at Stage 6 are **concrete and particular**. "We build this way" is a
Stage 6 rule. "We organize this way" is a Stage 6 rule. These rules apply to "us" but
not to "them."

The agent at Stage 6 can follow structural rules but cannot **reason about** structural
rules. The rule is followed because it is the rule. Questioning the rule is experienced
as a threat to the social order.

The transition from Stage 6 to Stage 7 occurs when the agent begins to question
structural rules — when it asks "but is this structural arrangement really correct?"
This is the shift from structure-following to structure-evaluation.

In human development, Stage 6 corresponds to the school-age child who internalizes
structural methods. "You have to build it this way" becomes "building it this way is
correct."

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** Cultural structural norms are the primary hierarchy mechanism. The tribe's
  building methods, organizational customs, and structural practices are the
  institutional framework of Stage 6.

- **UR:** The individual agent has internalized structural norms and follows them
  through guilt-based compliance.

- **LL:** Cultural institutions enforce structural norms through education,
  apprenticeship, and social pressure.

- **LR:** The workshop, the master's studio, the building site, the craft guild.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Rigid adherence to structural rules beyond their useful life.

- **Dark allergy:** Refusal to internalize any structural norms.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to a particular cultural structural method as
  universally correct.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting all cultural structural norms as arbitrary constraints.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Structure-following without evaluation:** The agent follows structural rules
  because they are the rules of the community.

- **Guilt-based compliance:** The agent feels guilt when it violates structural norms.

- **In-group hierarchy favoritism:** Structural norms apply within the group but not
  between-group.

- **Concrete rule application:** The agent applies structural rules literally, without
  considering context or exception.
